project.promise: The Stokes crew attempts extraordinary, easy-to-follow challenges across surprising game worlds, with real competition, cinematic scale and earned outcomes.
project.audience: Largest worldwide audience pool; broadly understandable and recognizably Stokes.

project.language: English first, designed for later localization.

claims.text: The swap test for borrowing a format: take the source channel's outliers and ask whether the concept keeps its novelty and humour with your subject substituted in. Formats rooted in specifically human relationships ('stuck with your ex') fail the test for non-players.

claims.text: In gaming, long uncut formats (event VODs, ranking/tier lists) produce deceptively high AVD with catastrophic APV : 12:23 AVD at 7.95% APV, and the lowest CTRs on the channel : so AVD alone will misidentify them as the channel's watchability leaders.
claims.caveat: Caveat: One channel and effectively one video : an anecdote, not a finding. The CTR half is untestable (no CTR data). The second gaming channel we hold (Channel B) has no retention curves at all, so there is no independent gaming replication available. The general warning that AVD misidentifies watchability leaders is better supported by the cross-channel WTH test (4524d4e423bd) than by this niche-specific version.
claims.unmeasured:
Not measurable by anything we currently compute No test in our battery measures this claim's variables, so it has never been quantified :
      so it stays a Warning on the strength of practitioner testimony. A failure mode is worth avoiding on good

claims.text: Upload timing derived from data can contradict audience intuition and still win: a gaming channel's audience peaked in the early morning rather than after school, and shifting to it produced the channel's best video in a long time and 64 million views in 28 days.
claims.caveat: Caveat: The claim is about matching a specific measured audience-online peak, and that peak is exactly the datum we lack : a channel's modal publish hour is not the same thing as its audience peak, so a null here does not refute the claim, it only shows there is no generic publish-hour effect. The 64M-view anecdote is a single video on a channel we do not hold; single-video before/after evidence cannot separate timing from the video itself.

shorts_formats.name: One spectacular myth, complete verdict

shorts_formats.hook: Lead with the hardest claim, then begin the easiest test immediately.
shorts_formats.production_need: Use only distinct filmed tests; fewer complete tests beat an inflated count.

shorts_formats.production_need: The source proves a visible constraint example, not this crew-prank variant; format is a launch test supported by long-form 12.

packaging.lead: Make a stranger understand the human promise before they recognize the game. Keep the game name as context, then earn the click with a familiar object, unequal stakes, an intriguing secret or a visible decision. The thumbnails carry cinematic scale; the page stays simple.
principles: Expectation match: the opening gameplay must establish the same object, scale and danger shown in the thumbnail. Generated concepts are planning images; replace unsupported elements with the finished playable build before upload.

Complement the title: a price title gets a tangible cheap/expensive object, a secret-room title gets the entrance, and a risk title gets the visible thing that can be lost. Avoid pasting the complete headline into the image.
Use one dominant subject and at most three visual groups. A repeated wall of cars counts as one coherent group; ten disconnected props do not.
Recognizable Stokes face, expressive but story-appropriate emotion, photographic creator cutout and a coherent cinematic game world. Rotate who is featured when the crew member drives the story.

Show functional spectacle: a course has a reachable finish, a room has an entrance, a race has matching directions and a giant experiment has an observable impact. Increase actual consequence before increasing a title number.
At phone size, identify the face, challenge object and information gap in a glance. Preserve silhouettes, color separation and readable minimal labels; check the duration-overlay corner.
Translate later: ordinary words, numerals, objects and movement do the work. Avoid lore, unexplained acronyms, fake review screenshots and English puns as the sole hook.

compositions.name: Value contrast
compositions.design: Two tangible versions of the same object, small/rough versus grand/polished; simple price anchors and one host.
compositions.gap: Does the expensive version actually solve the problem?
compositions.watchout: 01 compares supplied products; 04 follows unequal-budget builders. Game values must not masquerade as cash production spend.

compositions.name: Hidden entrance / revealed world
compositions.design: Ordinary exterior with one open hatch into a surprising large space; shushing host and a clearly different interior color.
compositions.gap: Where is it, how does it work, and will the crew discover it?
compositions.watchout: A cinematic cutaway must match a working entrance in the final filmed map.

compositions.name: Small team / overwhelming force
compositions.design: Big expressive host or small escape vehicle foreground; pursuit force receding into depth; readable destination.
compositions.gap: How could they possibly get away?
compositions.watchout: Actual participant/NPC counts and capture rules matter more than a decorative crowd.

compositions.name: Disaster and escape route
compositions.design: Recognizable cast in danger, one dominant wave/tornado and one visibly attainable safe area.
compositions.gap: Who makes it out and what has to be sacrificed?
compositions.watchout: No Los Santos dependency or unsupported disaster physics; use the real configured effect.

compositions.name: Impossible physical question
compositions.design: Host plus one unusual test object; repetition or scale difference supplies the apparent impossibility.
compositions.gap: Will the collision, jump or strange invention really work?
compositions.watchout: Do not spoil the final result or imply unverified stock-game behavior.

compositions.name: Dramatic irony / prank cause
compositions.design: Knowing operator contrasted with surprised crew and one visible cause: lever, wheel or altered vehicle.
compositions.gap: When will the crew realize what is happening?
compositions.watchout: Prank the mission rather than recycle unrelated loud reactions.

compositions.name: Dream fulfillment
compositions.design: Delighted creator/recipient and one enormous personal dream object or functioning build.
compositions.gap: What will the friends choose, and can the promise be fulfilled?
compositions.watchout: Name real versus virtual fulfillment; an unlimited real purchase headline needs an actual funded commitment.

compositions.name: Fair mystery / suspects
compositions.design: A performed incident, a readable suspect group and one clue; cinematic suspense without gore.
compositions.gap: Which friend did it and what clue did we miss?
compositions.watchout: The mystery family is mixed; casting and fair reveal must earn the title.

compositions.name: Risk versus kept reward
compositions.design: One valuable object visibly at risk, a big host reaction and a simple keep/risk decision.
compositions.gap: Will the player bank the reward or lose it trying for more?
compositions.watchout: Larger cash text alone is weak: the MrBeast Gaming prize family has a lower median than the best individual risk video.

compositions.name: Impossible route / prison
compositions.design: Tiny opening or finish framed by an enormous readable obstacle or enclosure; host foreground for scale.
compositions.gap: How can the crew cross or get out?
compositions.watchout: 14 is skill/attempts; 16 is cooperative clues/security. Their thumbnails can overlap, so titles and opening goals must distinguish them.

compositions.name: Game versus reality / journey

packaging.testing: Create at least five distinct thumbnail sketches per pilot (comparison, action, reveal, scale, consequence), then choose one finished direction. This document supplies one selected concept per episode, not five rendered variants per idea. For upload tests, keep the premise truthful, compare watch-time share where native tests provide it, log dates and exposure, and avoid calling tiny uncontrolled samples winners.

creative.lead: The broad audience watches a person attempt something clear; the gamer also enjoys the route, physics, build ingenuity or strategy. Introduce only the mechanic needed to understand the next consequence. A difficult game can hold a simple story.
hooks: Start with the wreck and supercar or the crew facing a hunter wall. A viewer can predict the obvious favorite before the first fair test.
Put the moving train and barrier in the same geography. Ask one concrete question, show the smallest failed test, then earn the bigger attempt.
Let the audience see the hidden operator before the crew notices the obstruction. The gap is when and how the friends discover the cause.
Show the wave or locked exit while naming one attainable safe destination. Establish who can still succeed and what they carry.
Give someone a reward they already care about, then offer one visible harder trial. Let the person deliberate instead of forcing a scripted risk.
Record a friend’s exact wish before building. The payoff is their use and reaction, not an endless tour of expensive objects.
Introduce a victim/object, suspects and one inspectable clue. Viewers should be able to form and revise an explanation.
Use a matched task/landmark in both worlds and an understandable finish. Their different constraints create the interest.
Show a familiar job, a crew member’s bad first decision and its consequence. Their attempt to recover links the jokes into a story.
story: The card’s three authored beats establish the image promise, objective/rule and first consequential attempt. No game-history lecture or obligatory cast roll call.
Demonstrate the minimum rules through a real attempt; show a failure that teaches viewers how success would work. Introduce personalities when their decisions matter.
Every sequence changes state: route lost, reward banked, clue found, room discovered, supply saved, design improved. Alternate progress with setbacks; remove repeated resets without new learning.
Account for what remains and why the last attempt is harder or more meaningful. Re-establish geography and stakes so a casual viewer can follow the outcome.
Resolve the actual challenge clearly, preserve the failure if that is what happened, then show the human reaction and fulfilled reward. No arbitrary extra twist after the main payoff.
presentation: Performed competition: a producer knows the rules, cast knows its role and the outcome remains earned. Use for races, pursuit, risk and obstacle attempts.
Authored environment with unscripted discovery: developers build the room/puzzle, audience sees selected clues, crew discovers it on camera. Use for secret rooms and prisons.
Performed story: clue logic, suspects and incident are authored; investigators and viewer deductions carry the mystery. Label clearly as a game-world story rather than a real crime.
Experiment documentary: predeclare conditions, preserve failures and show measured counts/settings. Cinematic replays clarify the result without replacing the test.
Crew comedy: normal job, meaningful score and recurring consequences. Plan playable situations rather than demand a joke at every cut.
IRL/game hybrid: match task scope, establish route and travel rules, capture both clocks. The differences between worlds are the entertainment, not a fairness issue hidden from viewers.
creative.cast: Alan and Alex anchor recognition. Rotate operator, skeptic, ambitious builder, nervous driver, strategist, guest judge and comic challenger across the crew. Give a supporting performer the consequential choice or payoff when it improves the episode; use the twins’ relationship only when it adds a specific story beat.
creative.localization: Record clean isolated dialogue, protect words from music, keep names consistent, retain text-free title/thumbnail alternatives, export graphics separately and write jokes that survive translation. Explain a GTA wanted level as “the pursuers are closing in” before expecting the star icon to do the work. Teach a Minecraft interaction by showing its consequence.
creative.audience_check: Before greenlight, a non-gamer should explain the objective, failure condition and final reward from the first 30 seconds. A gamer should identify at least one real ingenuity or skill layer. This is a proposed editorial acceptance test, not measured audience retention.
creative.launch_structure: Five per-person crossovers intercut into one shared Godzilla finale; Alex’s audience-uncertain prank; actual GTA 6 first-completion race and group release.

post_production.lead: Four real peer/main-channel videos were sent for automated footage analysis. The moment notes identify candidate hooks, reveals and decisions to inspect; they do not identify measured retention winners. Two analyses cover only introductory excerpts and one stops before the catalogue runtime. Source-linked timestamps make each observation reviewable.
post_production.gap: No private YouTube Studio CTR, retention curves or audience-segment data has been supplied for Stokes Gaming or the parent channel. No MoreNizarisaqt graph is imported as Stokes evidence. Automated scene indexing can misdescribe longer videos; verify the original footage before copying an editorial moment.
review: First-frame match: compare the thumbnail subject, opening environment and first spoken objective. Remove an unrelated cold open that postpones the promised challenge.
Geography: use a brief overhead/map when the viewer loses the destination, then return to character action. A string of close-up crashes cannot explain who is winning a chase.
State changes: annotate every new clue, decision, failure and gain. Cut repeated travel/reset footage when it changes neither understanding nor stakes.
Reactions: preserve the decision, consequence and response in order. Do not splice a different reaction onto the result for manufactured drama.
Payoffs: include the complete final attempt and real reward handoff. The viewer must know what happened before the cast celebrates.

Avoid: unexplained inventory jargon, repeated rule speeches, arbitrary difficulty without a goal, visually impressive builds that never function and expensive prizes that have no human decision attached.
measurement: Create an event log keyed to source timecode: opening promise, first attempt, rule explanation, travel, reveal, choice, setback, finale and outro.

With authorized Studio access, export the real curve and align it to the event log. Inspect the first 30 seconds, exits around repeated explanations and responses to each payoff; watch the footage around every candidate dip/peak.
Separate first-time and returning viewers where available, traffic sources, age of upload and video length. Lifetime public lift and retention percentage are different quantities.
A spike may be replay/confusion and a dip may be skipped dead time. Record a hypothesis, make one clear editorial change in the next comparable episode and check the outcome.

shorts_strategy.lead: Use standalone micro-stories that make a complete promise and show a result. Actual public Shorts examples below establish identifiable formats and raw reach, not a proven conversion system or age-controlled outlier lift. GTA myth examples come from two creators; Minecraft examples show a clear constraint and a hidden-build reveal.
shorts_strategy.distribution: For each long-form capture, deliberately record one self-contained myth test, one decisive crew reaction and one reveal or near-failure with enough vertical framing. Publish only clips with their own setup and payoff. Start with a small varied batch rather than filling a daily quota with incomplete teasers.
shorts_strategy.conversion: Attach the related long-form video where the platform permits and track engaged views, viewed-versus-swiped, actual retention, returning viewers and attributable long-form traffic with authorized analytics. A Short can have many public views and still attract viewers who never watch the launch channel’s episodes.
shorts_strategy.cadence: Working launch experiment: two strong Shorts around each of eight uploads, plus one native micro-experiment when capture capacity allows. Timing is a testable publishing plan, not an algorithm rule. Keep the long-form team’s edit bandwidth protected.
shorts_strategy.limitations: Five primary-title/author-verified examples; two Minecraft examples have provisional shelf classification because the Shorts page could not be retrieved. Older public counts are reach examples, not a claim of current format growth. No verified Shorts-to-long-form conversion data is available.

data_analysis.lead: The research uses the public Influint intelligence index, gaming theory/standing/rejection pages and five public channel catalogues, plus exact primary video metadata and capability sources. Authenticated API/private creator data was unavailable. The plan uses the system’s evidence labels and keeps theory, observed performance and creative hypotheses separate.
metrics: Influint reports views relative to publication-date nearby uploads. The exact neighbor count/value is not exposed. Preserve each row’s metric window; some displayed 28d labels conflict with the global lifetime description.
All 23 displayed repeated Stokes/MrBeast Gaming family memberships were read; medians, sample size, date range, recent subsets, best and weakest examples were recomputed from reported lifts.
2.0× is the declared qualifying threshold, with separate shape and ingredient matches. Adjacent examples, raw view counts and 1.97× secret-room evidence do not count as 2× proof.
Two channels can belong to the same creator ecosystem: Preston/Brianna are grouped together. Count channels and creator groups separately.
Automated timestamps are qualitative candidate observations, with incomplete analysis scope disclosed. They are not Studio retention measurements.
One independently generated selected concept per idea, exact prompt/reference IDs, image dimensions, hashes and recorded model availability. No image has a measured CTR result.
Incremental USD planning assumptions, separate per-video/one-time/monthly pools and unfunded real-prize liabilities. No contractor quote or approved cash budget is implied.
data_analysis.aspirations: 10M subscribers by January 1 remains an ambition. Score each video against 10M views in its own first 28 days, including December uploads maturing in January. These are targets, not forecasts.
data_analysis.next_data: Refresh public reference snapshots before selecting the next slate; preserve immutable snapshots and observed dates. Once the channel has comparable uploads and authorized analytics, build its own nearby-upload baseline rather than applying Stokes-main-channel views to a new gaming channel.
data_analysis.guidance: The two attached thumbnail PDFs informed expectation match, complementary text/visuals, one clear subject, restrained visual groups, mobile readability and appropriate emotion. Relevant frameworks include price/size comparison, action, hidden reveal, object repetition, landscape/map and transformation. Social/news UI is used only when it is genuine evidence; a decorative fake headline is not needed.
